title: 02. Tool Calling & MCP: Day 6 — Validation, Retries, and MCP
summary: Real agents make mistakes. A model might return an invoice total of $1,200,000 when the prompt said "small business invoice," or call a tool with malformed arguments.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Real agents make mistakes. A model might return an invoice total of `$1,200,000` when the prompt said "small business invoice," or call a tool with malformed arguments. Today you will harden your agents three ways: tune generation with **`model_settings`**, force retries with **`ModelRetry`** and validators, and extend your agent with external capabilities via the **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**. By the end, your agent will refuse bad answers, ask the model to try again, and read files off disk without you writing a single file-reading tool.

sections.title: model_settings — Per-Run Tuning
sections.body:
`model_settings` is a `ModelSettings` dict-like object that controls generation parameters. You can set defaults on the agent and override per run.

```python
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.settings import ModelSettings

# Defaults baked into the agent
agent = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    model_settings=ModelSettings(temperature=0.2, max_tokens=500, timeout=30),
)

# Override per run
result = await agent.run(
    "Brainstorm 10 name ideas for a coffee shop.",
    model_settings=ModelSettings(temperature=0.9, max_tokens=2000),
)
```

Supported keys (provider-dependent): `temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `timeout`, and `frequency_penalty`. Per-run settings merge with agent defaults — pass only what you want to override.

Two rules of thumb: set conservative defaults on the agent (`temperature=0.2`, `max_tokens=500`, `timeout=30`), then crank creativity on the specific runs that need it.

sections.title: Retry Logic with ModelRetry
sections.body:
Sometimes the model produces an answer that is technically valid but semantically wrong — an invoice total 100x too large, a date in the year 3024, a category that doesn't exist. You want to send the model a correction and ask it to try again.

Pydantic AI exposes this via the **`ModelRetry`** exception. Raise it inside a `result_validator`, a `@field_validator`, or a tool. Pydantic AI catches it, appends the error message to the conversation, and re-asks the model.

```python
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelRetry

@agent.result_validator
def reject_huge_totals(result: InvoiceResult) -> InvoiceResult:
    if result.total_usd > 100_000:
        # This message goes back to the model as a tool/result correction
        raise ModelRetry(
            f"Total ${result.total_usd} is too large for auto-approval. "
            "Re-extract the invoice; if the total really is over $100k, "
            "set needs_human_review=True instead."
        )
    return result
```

The model sees the error and gets another shot. Without a usage limit, this can loop forever — always set `usage_limit=` on `run()`.

sections.title: Example 1: Invoice Parser with result_validator
sections.body:
```python
# invoice_parser.py
import asyncio
from datetime import date
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelRetry

class Invoice(BaseModel):
    vendor: str
    invoice_date: date
    total_usd: float = Field(gt=0)
    needs_human_review: bool = False

invoice_agent = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    result_type=Invoice,
    system_prompt=(
        "Extract structured invoice data from the user's text. "
        "If the total exceeds $100,000, set needs_human_review=True "
        "and still return the parsed invoice."
    ),
)

@invoice_agent.result_validator
def validate_invoice(result: Invoice) -> Invoice:
    # Rule 1: future dates are not allowed
    if result.invoice_date > date.today():
        raise ModelRetry(
            f"invoice_date {result.invoice_date} is in the future. "
            "Re-read the invoice text and use the correct date."
        )
    # Rule 2: vendors must be at least 2 chars
    if len(result.vendor.strip()) < 2:
        raise ModelRetry("Vendor name is too short. Re-extract from the text.")
    return result

async def main() -> None:
    raw = """
    Acme Corp invoice #1234
    Date: 2024-05-01
    Total due: $4,250.00
    """
    result = await invoice_agent.run(raw, usage_limit=3)
    print(result.data.model_dump_json(indent=2))

asyncio.run(main())
```

Run it and the model produces a valid `Invoice`. Now feed it `Total due: $4,250,000.00` — the system prompt instructs the model to set `needs_human_review=True`. If the model forgets, you can add another validator that flips the flag automatically when `total_usd > 100_000` and re-raises.

sections.title: Field-Level Validators with Pydantic v2
Model Context Protocol (MCP)
sections.body:
The **Model Context Protocol** is an open standard (Anthropic-led) for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to LLMs via a uniform JSON-RPC interface. Instead of writing one tool per integration, you connect to an **MCP server** and Pydantic AI auto-discovers its tools.

Why it matters:

- **Composability.** A filesystem MCP server, a Postgres MCP server, a Slack MCP server — your agent gets all their tools by listing two connections.
- **Language-agnostic.** MCP servers can be written in TypeScript, Go, Rust — anything that speaks JSON-RPC over stdio or HTTP.
- **Reuse.** The same MCP server works with Claude Desktop, Cursor, Pydantic AI, LangChain, and any other MCP-aware client.

Pydantic AI ships two transports:

- **`MCPServerStdio`** — launches a subprocess and talks over stdin/stdout. The most common type for local servers.
- **`MCPServerHTTP`** — connects to a running HTTP/SSE MCP server. Used for remote or shared servers.

Install the filesystem server once:

```bash
npm install -g @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem
# or just use npx as shown below
```

sections.title: Example 2: File System Agent via MCP
sections.body:
```python
# fs_agent.py
import asyncio
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.mcp import MCPServerStdio

# Connect to the official filesystem MCP server, scoped to /tmp
fs_server = MCPServerStdio(
    "npx",
    args=["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/tmp"],
)

fs_agent = Agent(
    "openai:gpt-4o-mini",
    mcp_servers=[fs_server],
    system_prompt=(
        "You can read files, list directories, and search file contents "
        "via the filesystem tools. Always confirm before deleting anything."
    ),
)

async def main() -> None:
    # run_mcp_servers starts the subprocess(es) and tears them down on exit
    async with fs_agent.run_mcp_servers():
        # Create a sample file so the agent has something to read
        with open("/tmp/hello.txt", "w") as f:
            f.write("Hello from Pydantic AI + MCP!")

        result = await fs_agent.run(
            "List the files in /tmp, then read hello.txt and tell me its contents."
        )
        print(result.data)

asyncio.run(main())
```

When the agent starts, Pydantic AI queries the MCP server for its tool list and registers them as agent tools. The model then calls `read_file`, `list_directory`, `search_files` (or whatever the server exposes) exactly like agent-defined tools.

To use an HTTP MCP server:

```python
from pydantic_ai.mcp import MCPServerHTTP

remote_server = MCPServerHTTP("https://mcp.example.com/sse")
agent = Agent("openai:gpt-4o-mini", mcp_servers=[remote_server])

async with agent.run_mcp_servers():
    result = await agent.run("Use the remote tools to ...")
```

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
- **Infinite retry loops.** A validator that always rejects creates an infinite loop. Always pass `usage_limit=` (e.g., `usage_limit=3`) to `run()` when using `ModelRetry`.
- **Validator must raise `ModelRetry`, not return.** Returning a value from a validator passes through silently. Returning `None` or `False` does not retry — you must `raise ModelRetry("…")`.
- **Raising `ValueError` instead of `ModelRetry`.** Pydantic `ValueError` in a `result_validator` raises a `ValidationError` that aborts the run. Use `ModelRetry` to ask the model to try again.
- **MCP server must be running.** `MCPServerStdio` spawns it for you inside `run_mcp_servers()`. `MCPServerHTTP` assumes a server is already up — start it yourself or you get a connection refused.
- **MCP tool name collisions.** Two MCP servers exposing a tool with the same name (`read_file`, say) collide. Pydantic AI may raise or silently pick one. Prefix tool names by configuring the MCP server, or only enable one server at a time.
- **`temperature=0` is not deterministic.** Most providers still return slightly different outputs across calls due to floating point and routing. For true determinism, pin a specific model snapshot and use a deterministic seed if supported.
- **`max_tokens` truncates silently.** If your structured output gets cut off, parsing fails with a confusing error. Set `max_tokens` generously for structured-output agents.

sections.title: What's Next
sections.body: Day 7 takes everything you have learned — typed agents, tools, deps, streaming, validation, MCP — and ships it. You will build a multi-agent Co-Pilot where a router delegates to email, calendar, and task sub-agents; wrap it in a FastAPI service with sync and streaming endpoints; instrument it with Logfire; and write your first eval dataset. Day 7 closes Phase 1 and primes you for the 14-day project phase starting Day 8.
